title: Add Dijkstra pathfinding mode for Godot Navigation

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Closes https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/12664

This PR adds Dijkstra as a selectable pathfinding algorithm for Godot Navigation in both 2D and 3D.

A* remains the default pathfinding algorithm for performance and backwards compatibility. Dijkstra is added as an opt-in alternative for projects that need pathfinding based strictly on accumulated travel cost.

The implementation reuses the existing navmesh graph search structure and isolates the algorithm-specific behavior in the heuristic calculation. Besides that, we opted to refactor the navmesh corridor to reduce code duplication and make it easier to later implement other navigation algorithms.

Changes to the code:

 - Add PATHFINDING_ALGORITHM_DIJKSTRA to 2D and 3D navigation pathfinding enums.
- Expose Dijkstra in NavigationPathQueryParameters2D/3D.
- Expose Dijkstra in NavigationAgent2D/3D.
- Refactor navmesh path corridor search into shared helpers.
- Use a zero heuristic for Dijkstra pathfinding.
- Add documentation for the new enum value.
- Add navigation server tests for the new pathfinding mode.

This feature was tested both manually, in Editor using the NavigationAgent node in 2D and 3D and choosing Dijkstra as the pathfinding algorithm, and using the following commands:

```
scons platform=linuxbsd target=editor dev_build=yes tests=yes -j$(nproc)

./bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 --test --tc="*[NavigationServer2D]*"
./bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 --test --tc="*[NavigationServer3D]*"

```

The tests added were of two kinds:
1. To verify that Dijkstra returns a valid path.
2. To compare the performance of Dijkstra vs A*, showing Dijkstra preferring a lower cost route instead of relying on a distance-based heuristic like A*.
